name: Sudama
role: Childhood friend and devotee of Krishna
summary: Sudama, also called Kuchela, is the poor but gentle brahmin friend of Krishna from their school days. His visit to Krishna in Dvaraka with a small bundle of flattened rice is one of the most loved stories of friendship.
about: The Bhagavata Purana tells of a learned, contented brahmin friend of Krishna, whom later retellings call Sudama or Kuchela. He studied with Krishna at the ashram of the sage Sandipani, believed to be at Ujjain. He later lives in great poverty with his wife. At her urging he visits Krishna in Dvaraka, taking four handfuls of flattened rice as a gift. The text says Krishna welcomes him with great honour, eats some of the rice and gives him no wealth during the visit. On his way home Sudama finds his hut replaced by palaces, yet he stays unattached to riches. One tradition makes Sudama and Tulasi companions of Krishna in Goloka until a curse of Radha sent them to earth. Akshaya Tritiya is linked to this story.
kidSummary: Sudama is Krishna's old school friend. He was very poor, but he walked a long way to visit Krishna with a small gift of flattened rice. Krishna welcomed him warmly, and the story is told as the model of true friendship.

story.title: Friends at school
story.text: Sudama and Krishna study together at Sandipani's ashram. Once they go to gather firewood and get lost in a storm, but they hold hands until the teacher finds them.

story.title: A poor home
story.text: Years later Sudama lives in poverty with his wife. She tells him that Krishna, his old friend, is kind and could help, so he agrees to go.

story.title: A small gift
story.text: His wife begs four handfuls of flattened rice from neighbours and wraps them in an old cloth. Sudama carries it to Dvaraka and feels too shy to give it.

story.title: A king washes his feet
story.text: Krishna jumps up, hugs Sudama, washes his feet and sits him down. He takes the bundle, eats a handful with delight and reaches for another until Rukmini gently stops him.

story.title: The surprise at home
story.text: Sudama has asked for nothing, but when he reaches home his hut has become palaces. He thanks Krishna and lives simply, still thinking of his friend.

teaches: A small gift given with love is big
Do not ask for more than you need

facts.text: Kuchela, the other name of Sudama, is a Sanskrit word for someone dressed in bad or ragged clothes, a name that points to his poverty.
A popular retelling says Sudama quietly ate the food the teacher's wife packed for both boys while Krishna slept on his lap, then claimed the crunching was his teeth chattering from cold.
In the Bhagavata Purana Krishna rose from his queen's bed, hugged Sudama, wept with love, washed his feet and sprinkled the water on his own head.
Before touching the rice, Krishna told Sudama that he accepts even a leaf, flower, fruit or water offered with love, while grand gifts from those without devotion do not please him.
Sudama was too embarrassed to offer the rice, so he hid it. Krishna snatched the bundle, ate a handful and reached for a second.
Rukmini stopped Krishna from eating a second handful, saying one was already enough to make Sudama prosperous.

Porbandar in Gujarat, famous as Mahatma Gandhi's birthplace, is also said to be Sudama's birthplace and is called Sudamapuri. Its Shree Sudamaji Mandir is one of the few temples in India built in his name.
In the Bhagavata Purana, Krishna himself recalls to Sudama how the teacher's wife sent them for firewood, a storm struck, and they wandered in the dark until Sandipani found them at sunrise.

The Sanskrit verse (Bhagavata Purana 10.80.6) gives Krishna's poor friend no name; the English translation on Vedabase adds 'Sudama' in square brackets. The names Sudama and Kuchela come from later retellings.
One tradition says Sudama and Tulasi lived with Krishna in Goloka until a curse by Radha sent them to earth.
To reach Krishna in Dvaraka, the Bhagavata Purana says Sudama passed three guard posts and three gateways, walked by the homes of Krishna's devoted kin, and entered one of the palaces of his queens.
The goddess of fortune herself fanned the thin, ragged guest, says the Bhagavata Purana, and the people of the palace wondered what good deeds the unkempt brahmana had done to be served by the Lord.
Akshaya Tritiya is linked to Sudama's visit to Krishna at Dvaraka, when tradition says he received unlimited wealth as a boon from his friend.
Sudama's wife begged four handfuls of flattened rice from neighbouring brahmanas, tied them in a torn piece of cloth and sent them as his gift for Krishna, says the Bhagavata Purana.
The Malayalam poem Kuchelavritham was written at the suggestion of the Travancore king Marthanda Varma. About 96 of its 698 lines praise him and the Padmanabhaswamy Temple, and 132 describe Krishna.

In the school-days tale, Krishna answered Sudama's chattering-teeth excuse by saying he believed him, since he knew Sudama would never eat alone without sharing, and had only wanted to check the sound.

In Wikipedia's retelling of the Bhagavata story, Sudama found his hut replaced by several seven-storied palaces with gardens, while musicians welcomed him and his wife shone like Lakshmi as she wept for joy.
Though he now lived in great wealth, the Bhagavata Purana says Sudama stayed detached and kept singing Krishna's praises, and in time let go of every worldly tie.
When their teacher Sandipani found the boys after the stormy night, the Bhagavata Purana says he blessed them, wishing their learning would never lose its meaning in this world or the next.
In a summary of the Bhagavata story, Krishna, Balarama and their friend Sudama learned each lesson at Sandipani's school after hearing it only once, then asked their teacher what fee he wished for.

quiz.q: What gift did Sudama bring for Krishna?
quiz.why: He brought a small bundle of flattened rice.

quiz.q: Who stopped Krishna from eating a second handful of rice?
quiz.why: Rukmini said one handful was enough.

quiz.q: Where did Krishna and Sudama study?
quiz.why: Both studied with the sage Sandipani.

quiz.q: What happened to Sudama's hut after his visit?
quiz.why: He found luxurious palaces when he returned.

quiz.q: How does the Bhagavata Purana introduce Krishna's poor friend?
options: As a brahmana friend of Krishna
quiz.why: The verse gives no name; Sudama and Kuchela come from later retellings.

quiz.q: How many handfuls of flattened rice did Sudama's wife collect for Krishna?
quiz.why: The Bhagavata Purana says she begged four handfuls and tied them in a torn cloth.
